title: Mitigate misrouted traffic caused by stale policy cache + variant compatibility mismatch
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-26 we observed a spike in 5xx errors and elevated latency across multiple regions for several high-throughput customers. Root cause analysis shows two concurrent failures that combined to cause a cascading cross-region retry storm: 1) a stale in-memory policy cache that was not invalidated after a policy push, which led the smart router to evaluate an outdated policy ordering for a subset of requests; and 2) a variant compatibility schema mismatch between the routing layer and the model metadata service (versionedVariant vs variantTag), which allowed selection of an incompatible quantized variant for GPU types that cannot run the chosen kernel, triggering runtime OOMs and immediate 500s.

Systems involved:
- Smart routing service (policy evaluation + cache)
- Variant metadata service (model catalog)
- Serving runtime pool (GPU clusters in us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1)
- Client retry layer and region failover policy
- Observability dashboards & alerting

Impact:
- Customers: 6% of production requests for affected models returned 5xx for ~18 minutes peak, with increased tail latency for the following 30 minutes as retries saturated other regions.
- Internal: autoscaling in multiple regions triggered emergency capacity bursts, temporarily exceeding burst budgets and increasing cost.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Hotfix deployed to routing service to prefer current config store on policy evaluation and bypass local cache for 5 minutes (rollbackable) — reduced window where stale policy was used.
- Emergency validation in metadata service to block variants that declare incompatible runtime ABI (added a temporary hard fail).
- Adjusted client-side retry to add randomized exponential backoff and reduced cross-region failover aggressiveness.

Root cause (combined):
1) Policy cache invalidation: after a configuration push the cache eviction path was a best-effort async walk; under a race the router continued using an older policy ordering for some instances. That older policy overlapped with a newly-introduced model-family rule which changed routing precedence.
2) Variant schema mismatch: the routing layer looked up "variantId" mapping but the metadata service had a rolling change replacing "variantId" with "versionedVariant" for new entries. This subtle mismatch meant the router considered two variants as compatible when they were not (the logic compared family strings instead of runtime ABI and kernel compatibility).
3) Retry amplification: when OOMs occurred, the router returned 5xx and the client-level failover retried to other regions without a global circuit breaker, causing a brief capacity cascade.

Why this escaped automated checks:
- Integration tests assert presence of variant keys but not strict runtime ABI compatibility.
- Policy push tests validate store-write but not the in-memory cache consistency under race conditions.
- No end-to-end chaos tests that exercised simultaneous config changes + metadata schema rollouts + cross-region retries.
